## 🔑 Key Takeaways

- **69 years of progress** separate these two satellites.
- Sputnik 1 was a bare-bones **beach-ball-sized sphere** with no scientific instruments — just a radio beeper. SMILE is a sophisticated multi-instrument observatory built jointly by two major space agencies.

- The leap from Sputnik 1 to today represents one of the most dramatic technological evolutions in human history. 🚀

---

## 🔴 SPUTNIK 1 — The First Satellite (1957)

Sputnik 1 was the first artificial Earth satellite, launched into an elliptical low Earth orbit by the Soviet Union on **4 October 1957**.

### Key Specs:
| Feature | Details |
|---|---|
| **Shape** | Polished metal sphere |
| **Diameter** | 58 cm (23 in) |
| **Mass** | 83.6 kg (184 lbs) |
| **Instruments** | 2 radio transmitters (1W each) + 3 batteries + ventilator |
| **Antennas** | 4 external whip antennas (2.4–2.9 m long) |
| **Orbit type** | Elliptical Low Earth Orbit (LEO) |
| **Orbital period** | ~96 minutes |
| **Apogee / Perigee** | 947 km / 228 km |
| **Orbital inclination** | 65.1° |
| **Speed** | ~29,000 km/h |
| **Operational life** | 21 days (batteries depleted) |
| **Total time in orbit** | 92 days (~1,400 orbits) |
| **Mission** | Radio signal broadcast, pressure/temperature monitoring |

The satellite consisted of a pressurized, highly polished aluminium shell containing two 1W transmitters, three silver-zinc batteries, and one ventilator, connected to four whip antennas — two of 2.4 m and two of 2.9 m in length.

It achieved an orbit with an apogee of 940 km and a perigee of 230 km, circling Earth every 96 minutes.

The satellite's orbit decayed 92 days after launch, having completed about **1,400 orbits** of the Earth over a cumulative distance of **70 million kilometres**.

The satellite's success was unanticipated by the United States, precipitating the "Sputnik crisis" and triggering the start of the **Space Race**.

---

## 🔵 SMILE — One of the Latest Satellites (May 2026)

The SMILE spacecraft lifted off on a Vega-C rocket from Europe's Spaceport in French Guiana on **19 May 2026**.

### Key Specs:
| Feature | Details |
|---|---|
| **Full Name** | Solar Wind Magnetosphere Ionosphere Link Explorer |
| **Agencies** | ESA (Europe) + CAS (China) — joint mission |
| **Launch vehicle** | Vega-C rocket |
| **Orbit type** | Highly elliptical polar orbit |
| **Apogee / Perigee** | ~121,000 km (North Pole) / ~5,000 km (South Pole) |
| **Instruments** | 4 scientific instruments (X-ray camera, UV camera, particle & magnetic field detectors) |
| **Comms** | X-band communications system |
| **Power** | Deployable solar panels |
| **Planned lifetime** | 3 years |
| **Mission** | Study Earth's magnetosphere & solar wind interaction |

SMILE is a joint mission between ESA and the Chinese Academy of Sciences. Using X-ray and UV cameras, as well as particle and magnetic field detectors, it will give humankind its first complete look at how Earth reacts to streams of particles and bursts of radiation from the Sun.

Over the course of a month, its propulsion module will bring the spacecraft to its nominal orbit — a polar orbit with apogee and perigee altitudes of around **121,000 km** above the North Pole and **5,000 km** above the South Pole, respectively.

This is the first time a mission has been jointly designed, implemented, launched, and operated by ESA and China.

Following its launch, SMILE will spend around one month travelling to its operational orbit, with scientific data collection expected to officially begin in **September 2026**.

---

|---|---|---|
| **Launch Date** | October 4, 1957 | May 19, 2026 |

| **Instruments** | 2 basic radio transmitters | 4 advanced scientific instruments |
| **Orbit altitude** | 228–947 km (LEO) | 5,000–121,000 km (highly elliptical) |
| **Power source** | Silver-zinc batteries (lasted 21 days) | Solar panels (3-year mission) |
| **Communications** | Simple radio pulses (20 & 40 MHz) | X-band communications system |
| **Mission purpose** | Prove orbital spaceflight was possible | Study Earth's magnetosphere & space weather |
| **Scientific output** | Minimal (temperature, pressure, radio signals) | Cutting-edge X-ray & UV observations of Earth's magnetic shield |
| **Operational life** | 21 days | Designed for 3 years |

---

## 🔑 Key Takeaways

- **69 years of progress** separate these two satellites.
- Sputnik 1 was a bare-bones **beach-ball-sized sphere** with no scientific instruments — just a radio beeper. SMILE is a sophisticated multi-instrument observatory built jointly by two major space agencies.
- Sputnik orbited just **228–947 km** above Earth; SMILE reaches up to **121,000 km** — over 100× higher.
